rationale: The workflow already contains a Gradle dependency cache (actions/cache@v6 caching ~/.gradle/caches, ~/.gradle/wrapper, and .git/modules, keyed on gradle files with restore-keys), which is exactly the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache optimization. That pattern's own contraindication "An equivalent cache already exists" applies, so adding another cache step would be redundant rather than an improvement. No other evidence-supported pattern has its preconditions clearly satisfied without contraindication: there is no matrix (P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST), no scheduled workflow (P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE), no Bazel build (P-LIT-BAZEL-*), no Python/pip dependency install (P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE pip example), and no test-selection/prioritization data. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT risks false failures on cold/cache-miss Gradle builds without sufficient safe-duration history. Build and test coverage is preserved as-is.
